overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the chair may limit public participation, so ruling a speaker's off-notice topic out of order was within discretion. The complaint was resolved by informal action.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee did not allow public participation at its September 15 meeting, after the chair ruled a speaker's topic (an Assistant Superintendent hiring process) was off the notice.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, because it is within the Chair’s discretion to limit public participation during a meeting, the Chair did not violate the Open Meeting Law by preventing the complainant from addressing the Committee during the September 15 meeting.
